projects.metaDescription: Vozokany, post.work and Viki: software for farm operations, managed AI agents and specification-driven development by Matej Lukášik.
projects.heroDescription: Software built for **real workflows**, from farm operations to AI-assisted development.

items.title: Vozokany
items.preview: I **replaced a farm’s email-based ordering** with a lean software solution. This made ordering products more convenient and led to **increased sales**.
items.description:
I built Vozokany after experiencing the farm’s ordering process as a customer. Offers arrived by email as images containing products and prices. Customers had to **compose their orders manually**, leaving the farmer to process the replies.

I created a working prototype and developed it through ongoing feedback from the farmer. It grew into a system for weekly offers, online ordering, harvest planning and packing. One important simplification was giving each customer a **single editable weekly order** until a defined deadline, resolving confusion around repeated submissions. I owned the idea, product decisions, design, development using AI, deployment and ongoing maintenance.

The farm now **uses Vozokany every week** to send offers and receive orders. The farmer reports that customers order more regularly, which has **increased revenue**.
items.ownership: I designed and built the application, its Rust/TypeScript API contract, executable business specifications and release verification.

items.title: post.work
items.preview: I’m building post.work for small businesses that want to **delegate work to AI** without taking on its setup and maintenance. I designed the experience around assigning tasks, **inspecting results in existing tools** and approving the work. I own the product decisions, customer experience, integrations and operation.
items.description:
post.work grew out of my work helping small businesses put AI agents to use. They wanted to **delegate tasks, review the results and approve the work**, while someone else handled setup, integrations and ongoing maintenance.

I built a managed workspace around Hermes, which provides the underlying agent engine. Each business gets an **agent connected to its existing tools** through a simple interface. I designed the customer experience around delegating work and reviewing results, with the technical configuration and infrastructure handled as part of the service.

**Verifiable outcomes** were central to the product: an email draft in Mailchimp, posts in Later, or a Shopify page that the customer can open and inspect. This makes the result tangible and gives the customer a clear basis for feedback and approval. I owned the idea, product decisions, design, development using AI, integrations, deployment and ongoing operation.
items.ownership: I’m building the workspace, agent integrations, runtime lifecycle and recovery mechanisms around Hermes.

items.title: Viki
items.preview: I built Viki to **make unwritten business rules explicit and reviewable** before implementation. It helps people and coding agents work from a shared specification, with AI surfacing conflicts and questions for **human review**.
items.description:
Viki grew out of a proposal for a document-generation system. The business rules lived largely in an employee’s head, and we needed a shared place to make them explicit, discuss them and **agree on how the software should behave**.

I built Viki around concepts, features and human-readable Gherkin scenarios. Stakeholders describe a change in conversation, and Viki examines it against the existing specification, surfaces potential conflicts and asks clarifying questions. It helps turn the request into proposed changes that people can **review and approve before passing them to a coding agent** for implementation and verification.

Viki is the specification layer of a software factory: **a shared source of truth** connecting stakeholder decisions with the software being built. I developed it alongside Vozokany, using a real application’s business rules to ground the workflow. I owned the idea, product decisions, design, development using AI, deployment and ongoing maintenance.
items.ownership: I built the Go/React application, scoped agent tools and the import pipeline that validates repository specifications and verification evidence.

about.heroDescription: I help companies solve business problems with the right mix of bespoke software, automation, and AI.
about.bioText:
My strength is asking the questions that **bring clarity to complex, loosely defined problems**. When people come to me with competing ideas, requirements, feedback and constraints, I listen and help define what matters: the problem to solve, **what is worth building**, what would add complexity without value and what we still need to understand.

I **take responsibility for a feature or product** from that first conversation through design, implementation, release and improvement. I get to know the customers, business and existing systems, make the necessary decisions and tradeoffs, and **stay involved after launch** to understand what works and what needs improving.

I’ve spent the past **ten years working remotely** with small and medium-sized companies. I value autonomy, trust and **clear asynchronous communication**. I take initiative, communicate decisions and keep the people I work with informed.

I live in Trnava, Slovakia, and love spending time with my family—walking in nature, solving escape rooms, or going out for tea and cookies. I’m fascinated by ancient Greece, philosophy, and questions of conviction, ambition and free will. Steven Pressfield’s Gates of Fire and Tides of War are particular favourites. I believe in being the author of your own story and enjoying the ride with the people you love.
about.principle1Description: Open source or managed, self-hosted or cloud — I recommend what fits your team, budget, and security requirements.
about.principle2Description: I involve your team throughout delivery. The goal is for you to own the system and keep improving it.
about.principle3Description: First we validate one useful use case. We measure results and expand only what works.
about.techDescription: The right technical solution depends on the workflow. Sometimes a lightweight automation is enough; other times it takes a RAG system or a custom AI agent connected to existing tools. What they share are clear rules, controlled access, measurable results, and a team that knows how to use the solution.

faq.question: We don’t know whether we need new software, automation, or AI. Is it worth getting in touch?
faq.answer: Yes. Send me a message about the workflow or software problem and its business impact. We can then determine whether an Assessment Sprint is the right next step.

faq.question: Do we need to replace our current software?
faq.answer: Usually not. I first look for ways to improve or connect the systems that already work. I recommend replacing software only when the current system is holding the business back and the value of replacing it is clear.

faq.question: How long does an implementation take?
faq.answer: It depends on the problem, existing systems, and risk involved. The Assessment Sprint defines the recommended scope, success metric, and realistic implementation plan before you commit to the build.

faq.question: How do we know whether the solution is creating real value?
faq.answer: Before implementation, we agree on what should improve: time, cost, error rates, quality, or service speed. If the result cannot be measured credibly, we narrow the project or do not proceed.

faq.question: How do you handle data security?
faq.answer: We start with data, permissions, and deployment boundaries. The first version should use only the minimum necessary access, clear rules for sensitive data, and human review where the risk is higher. With security, slower and steadier is better.

faq.question: Do we need our own technical team?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. I can handle the technical side. Someone technical on your team helps with long-term maintenance and ownership, but the first project can start without an internal developer.

faq.question: What technology do you use?
faq.answer: I choose the technology only after understanding the problem and existing systems. The solution may be bespoke software, an automation, an AI agent, or a combination. The deciding factors are fit, reliability, security, operating cost, and maintainability.

faq.question: What happens after handoff?
faq.answer: Once the solution works, your team gets the operating rules, training, and enough context to use it safely. The goal is capability, not dependency. If useful, we can keep improving the solution together.
